title: Compact-context ideas + reading notes (scratchpad)
content:
Quick brain dump from last week of reading + small experiment plans. Mostly scratch — messy.

Goal: collect ideas for 'compact context' strategies that keep high retrieval/recall for LLMs while reducing KV-cache size and per-request latency. Useful for low-cost Dedicated and Private deployments where GPU memory is limited.

Papers/blogs skimmed (notes):
- " + "Sparse Composite Memory (arXiv) — idea: multi-resolution slots, only fetch top-k fine slots for active token windows. Good for long sessions but tricky to integrate with continuous batching. Notes: evaluate slot allocation overhead vs latency; possible policy: allocate fine slots for recent N tokens + coarse summary slots for older history.
- " + "Vector-stitching blog (distilled) — cheap anchors + bloom-like membership checks to avoid KV fetches for irrelevant segments. Implementation thought: precompute 64-bit signatures for chunks and put in an L0 filter per shard. Low overhead but needs collision analysis.
- " + "KV quantization/compaction paper — per-layer PCA on KV vectors to cut memory by 4x with small quality loss on retrieval tasks. Risk: PCA re-computation when model updates; tradeoffs: recompute offline during rollout window.

My hypotheses:
1) Hybrid chunking (overlap windows + anchor sketches) can drop effective cache size by ~3x for chat workloads with >2k tokens while holding reply quality.
2) Lightweight per-request filter (64-bit signatures) will reduce KV fetches significantly in high-turn environments (chatbots) with high locality.
3) Aggressive per-layer low-rank compaction will require per-model calibration (eval sets) to avoid producing hallucinations when rollouts change model scale.

Mini-experiment ideas (fast to run):
- Baseline: run convo traces (open-sourced chat logs) through our local KV cache sim + full fetch. Measure tokens/fetches, latency estimate.
- Add signature-filter: 64-bit Murmur hash of chunk embedding bins; simulate false-positive rate and blocked fetches; measure quality with BLEU/ROUGE on retrieval-based QA.
- PCA compaction: compress KV values to 128-d per layer, reconstruct at inference; run small eval suite (10 prompts each) to check deltas.

Practical notes / pitfalls:
- Batching: many of these tricks change request-level variance; need to account for batching window effects and tail latency when combining with continuous batching runtime.
- Eviction policies: LRU is suboptimal for chat — recency+importance score (attention-weighted) might be better but requires extra tracking. Keep an eye on storage/compute overhead.
- Consistency across Dedicated vs Private: For Private (on-prem) customers, we should provide both 'safe' presets (less compression) and 'aggressive' presets with clear regression monitoring.

Action list (next week):
- Prototype signature filter simulation (Devon) — target: synthetic trace sim + false positive curve. Owner: Devon. ETA: 2026-09-21.
- Small PCA compression experiment (Ivy) — pick 2 small models, run reconstruction QA. Owner: Ivy. ETA: 2026-09-24.
- Draft a short one-pager for Solutions Engineering on tradeoffs (Harper) — link to experiments + suggested defaults. Owner: Harper. ETA: 2026-09-28.

Open questions / TODOs to think through:
- What metrics should we expose in Console to help customers choose compression presets? (cost-per-token, recall@k, fallback-rate, cache-hit-efficiency)
- If we introduce lost-precision artifacts, what rollback/auto-fallback policy should we implement at runtime? Canary + rapid fallback to uncompressed variant seems necessary.

Links and quick refs (to copy into PRD later):
- arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.XXXX (placeholder — replace with exact ids)
- internal GH experiment: https://github.com/redwood-internal/context-cache-experiments (branch: compact-signatures)
- slack convo: #kv-cache-research thread (pinned messages)

Random notes to self:
- Try implementing a tiny Rust prototype for signature filter to test CPU overhead (we have E2 kernels for low-latency ops).
- When writing evals, include safety checks for 'incoherent' completions after compression. Use human-in-the-loop for 50 examples.

End of dump. This doc will be cleaned up into a short internal note for product/solutions if the experiments show promise.
